authoredNote: Authored BEFORE the `part_of` reading landed, so the pre-change run is a FAILING run (2 expected `part_of` edges, 0 actual) and a regression is visible. Line numbers were transcribed from the numbered source before any run: the `path` KEY's line is the site of the target name — 6 (`path = "terragrunt-root.hcl"`), 11 (`path = "./lib/terragrunt-library.hcl"`) — matching this analyzer's own attribute-keyed convention for `imports`/`overrides`/`inherits`. The four near misses (computed path 17, interpolated template 22, unnamed include 27, remote-state config path 35) and the two read-only neighbours (read_terragrunt_config 42, module source 48) were checked to produce NO `part_of` row after the change.
rationale: `part_of` is the textual-inclusion relation: the included unit's members become members of the INCLUDING document's configuration. terragrunt `include` is the one HCL construct that does that — terragrunt MERGES the included file's blocks into the child config (measured over the whole admitted population: 287 include blocks, 279 literal `path` values of which 28 name an existing tracked file, 8 computed; script/m14/hcl-extended-census.ts). The edge's target is the INCLUDED FILE'S ROOT-MODULE SYMBOL (its file stem — the same spelling `documentName()` gives every HCL file's root symbol), never the written path: the arbiter resolves a target string against symbol names and has no space for a filesystem path, and a path target resolves 0 rows. The written path is kept in `metadata.partPath` where a reader can check it against the source line, and `metadata.partRole` is MANDATORY on every `part_of` row. The near misses are pinned as FORBIDS rather than expected absences, because each is a DIFFERENT fact that a careless walker would publish as this one: a function-call path and an interpolated path are computed values (no file this parse can name), an include with no `path` names nothing, `terraform_remote_state` READS another stack's state (not a splice of it), `read_terragrunt_config()` READS a config at runtime, and a `module` block is a separate unit addressed `module.NAME.*` (inclusion by reference, never a textual merge — the module/`source` split the lane measured separately: 2,042 sites, 941 local, 496 registry, 193 vcs). An `include` whose written path names a file ABSENT from the project is deliberately NOT refused here: absence is not knowable in a pure AST pass, so those sites are published and counted as the arm's unresolved wall rather than guessed away.

a relative path with a directory component: the target is still the BASENAME's stem, not the path — `./lib/terragrunt-library.hcl` is not a symbol

the expression-as-target variant of the same fabrication, in case a future rule publishes the raw expression text
INTERPOLATED PATH. The static halves of `"${get_terragrunt_dir()}/root.hcl"` are not a filename; the target here is a value computed at runtime
THE TEMPLATE-LITERAL LEAK. Reading the `template_literal` child of an interpolated quoted_template yields the static segment; publishing `root` from line 22 would be a name this parse cannot know
ABSENT TARGET — the grammar permits `include` with no `path` attribute; a block that names no file includes nothing
a remote-state data source READS another stack's state; it does not splice that stack's configuration into this file
the remote state's own `config.path` names a STATE FILE, not a configuration unit: reading state is not textual inclusion
a part_of to a state file would assert a splice of serialized state into this config — a fact the tree contradicts
`read_terragrunt_config()` is a FUNCTION CALL that reads a config at runtime; the call's argument is a path expression, not a spliced unit
the function's argument must not be published as a part either: 0 rows for this name anywhere in the fixture

MODULE INCLUSION IS NOT A TEXTUAL SPLICE. A module source is a separate unit addressed `module.NAME.*`; it earns `imports`, never `part_of` — the discriminator this lane measured on 2,042 module-source sites
PATH-SHAPED TARGET. The arbiter resolves target strings against symbol names; the written path belongs in metadata.partPath, never in the target
